facts.statement: The genus is known only from a single tarsometatarsus described by Lambrecht in 1929.
facts.quote: It remains known from the single tarsometatarsus described in 1929 by Lambrecht

facts.statement: Neogaeornis lived approximately 70 to 67 million years ago.
facts.quote: It lived about 70-67 million years ago.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Neogaeornis spans the Maastrichtian stage from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Neogaeornis is classified as a controversial prehistoric genus of diving bird.
facts.quote: Neogaeornis is a controversial prehistoric genus of diving bird.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic studies suggest Neogaeornis is a basal loon.
facts.quote: Most recent phylogenetic studies seem to favour its position as a basal loon.

facts.statement: A 2017 study placed Neogaeornis in the family Vegaviidae alongside Polarornis, Australornis, and Vegavis.
facts.quote: In 2017 a phylogenetic study Agnolín and colleagues have found Neogaeornis to be stem-anseriforms along with Polarornis, Australornis and Vegavis in the family Vegaviidae.

facts.statement: Gerald Mayr argued that Neogaeornis may not belong to the family Vegaviidae because the specimen exhibits traits of other bird groups.
facts.quote: Gerald Mayr suggested that it is uncertain whether Neogaeornis belongs to the family since the specimen shows traits of other bird groups including those of podicipediform and gaviiform

facts.statement: The taxonomic placement of Neogaeornis remains controversial due to uncertainty regarding its evolutionary relationships.
facts.quote: It is controversial because of its uncertain placement.
Neogaeornis is a controversial prehistoric genus of diving bird.

rejected.statement: The only known species, Neogaeornis wetzeli, was described from fossils found in the Quiriquina Formation of Chile.
rejected.quote: The single known species, Neogaeornis wetzeli, was described from fossils found in the Campanian to Maastrichtian Quiriquina Formation of Chile.
